test_metadata.name: Speech Coach Diagnostic Test
test_metadata.description: Unified diagnostic assessment for identifying English learner weaknesses in Pronunciation and Grammar.

single_word_test.purpose: Detect voiceless dental fricative substitution (e.g., pronouncing /θ/ as /t/, /f/, or /s/)
Detect voiced dental fricative substitution (e.g., pronouncing /ð/ as /d/, /v/, or /z/)
Detect voiced labiodental fricative confusion (e.g., pronouncing /v/ as /w/ or /b/)
Detect voiced labial-velar approximant confusion (e.g., pronouncing /w/ as /v/)
Detect voiced alveolar approximant/liquid substitution (e.g., pronouncing /r/ as /l/ or /w/)
Detect voiced alveolar lateral approximant/liquid substitution (e.g., pronouncing /l/ as /r/)
Detect voiceless postalveolar fricative de-palatalization (e.g., pronouncing /ʃ/ as /s/)
Detect voiceless postalveolar affricate reduction (e.g., pronouncing /tʃ/ as /ʃ/ or /t/)
Detect voiced postalveolar affricate substitution/devoicing (e.g., pronouncing /dʒ/ as /tʃ/ or /z/)
Detect voiced alveolar fricative devoicing (e.g., pronouncing /z/ as /s/)
Detect voiced velar nasal substitution (e.g., pronouncing /ŋ/ as alveolar /n/ or /ŋg/)
Detect long vowel shortening (e.g., pronouncing long /iː/ as short /ɪ/)

minimal_pair_test.purpose: Identify short vs. long front vowel duration and quality confusion
Identify voiceless vs. voiced labiodental fricative confusion
Identify lateral vs. central liquid consonant confusion
Identify voiceless dental fricative vs. alveolar sibilant confusion
Identify labial-velar approximant vs. labiodental fricative confusion
Identify short mid-front vowel vs. diphthong vowel confusion
Identify near-open front vs. open-mid front vowel confusion
Identify voiced vs. voiceless postalveolar affricate confusion

sentence_reading_test.text: They will travel to the west valley this Thursday.
Please read the blue book under the large table.
The thin sheep sleeping in the shed is very light.
We want to visit a beautiful right-hand road.
He thought the red car was really fast and clean.
She specifically decided to buy a cheap yellow cup yesterday.

tongue_twister_test.text: I thought a thought, but the thought I thought wasn't the thought I thought I thought.
A loyal warrior roller skates rarely.
tongue_twister_test.target_sound: /r/ and /l/ liquid alternation in complex words

tongue_twister_test.text: Which witch wished to watch a wrist watch?
Pad kid poured curd pulled cod.

speaking_prompts.prompt: Describe your typical daily routine from morning to night.
Tell me about a memorable trip or vacation you took in the past.
What are your personal and professional goals for the next year?
Imagine you are looking out your window right now. Describe what is happening outside.
Talk about your family members. Mention what each person does for work or school.
If you could have any pet, which animal would you choose and why? Describe a typical day with it.
Describe the layout of your bedroom or living room, explaining where the furniture is located.
Imagine you are interviewing a famous celebrity. Ask them three interesting questions about their life.
Compare living in a busy metropolitan city versus living in a quiet countryside. Which do you prefer and why?
If you won a million dollars tomorrow, what would you do with the money?
Create a short story about a brave astronaut. Make sure each sentence clearly states who did what.
Explain why you decided to learn English, using words like 'because', 'although', and 'since'.

th_sound.what_is_measured: Accuracy in articulating voiceless /θ/ ('think') and voiced /ð/ ('this') sounds in words and connected speech.

beginner.criteria: Frequent substitutions of /θ/ with /t/, /f/, or /s/, and /ð/ with /d/, /v/, or /z/. Sounds are completely missing or distorted in most sentences.

intermediate.criteria: Occasional correct production in simple words, but prone to regression or substitution in fast speech, tongue twisters, or complex sentences.

advanced.criteria: Consistently correct production of dental fricatives in all environments, including connected speech and tongue twisters, with natural airflow.

vw_confusion.what_is_measured: Distinction between voiced labiodental fricative /v/ and voiced labial-velar approximant /w/.

beginner.criteria: Systematically conflates /v/ and /w/ (e.g. saying 'west' for 'vest' or 'very' as 'wery'). Labiodental contact is missing for /v/, or lip rounding is missing for /w/.

intermediate.criteria: Understands the distinction and produces them correctly in isolation, but merges them when they appear in close proximity (e.g. 'west valley').

advanced.criteria: Clear and distinct articulation of /v/ and /w/ in all contexts with natural transitions.

rl_confusion.what_is_measured: Accuracy in producing /r/ and /l/ liquid sounds and maintaining their contrast.

beginner.criteria: Severe substitution where /r/ becomes /l/ (or /w/) and /l/ becomes /r/, leading to high intelligibility issues in minimal pairs like 'light' vs 'right'.

intermediate.criteria: Can differentiate /r/ and /l/ in initial positions, but struggles with consonant clusters (e.g., 'blue', 'read') or tongue twisters (e.g., 'red lorry, yellow lorry').

advanced.criteria: Precise articulation of both liquids across all word positions, clusters, and challenging speech patterns.

long_vowels.what_is_measured: Acoustic duration and quality distinction of English long vowels (/iː/, /uː/, /ɑː/, /ɔː/, /ɜː/).

beginner.criteria: Regularly shortens long vowels, causing semantic confusion in pairs like 'sheep'/'ship' or 'beach'/'bitch'.

intermediate.criteria: Correctly elongates vowels in emphasized single words, but loses appropriate duration in fluid, connected sentence reading.

advanced.criteria: Maintains proper vowel length and distinct vowel quality naturally in all spoken contexts.

short_vowels.what_is_measured: Quality and articulation accuracy of short lax vowels (/ɪ/, /e/, /æ/, /ʌ/, /ʊ/, /ɒ/).

beginner.criteria: Frequently collapses short vowels into a single neutral sound or merges them with long counterparts (e.g., confusing 'bad' /æ/ and 'bed' /e/).

intermediate.criteria: Accurate with basic short vowels (/ɪ/, /e/) but struggles with neutral /ʌ/ vs /æ/ or /ʊ/ in longer words or rapid sentences.

advanced.criteria: Clean, distinct short vowel articulation with appropriate tongue height and mouth openness.

stress.what_is_measured: Placement of lexical word stress on appropriate syllables and sentence-level prominence on content words.

beginner.criteria: Monotone rhythm or incorrect syllable stress on common multi-syllable words (e.g., pronouncing 'specifically' or 'decided' with flat or misplaced stress).

intermediate.criteria: Places word stress correctly on familiar vocabulary but lacks proper sentence stress, resulting in an unnatural, disjointed speech rhythm.

advanced.criteria: Uses natural syllable stress and sentence-level contrastive stress, producing clear English speech rhythm (stress-timed rhythm).

fluency.what_is_measured: Smoothness, pacing, linking, and lack of unnatural pauses or hesitations in reading and speaking.

beginner.criteria: Extremely slow speech rate, word-by-word reading, frequent long pauses, high density of filler sounds ('uh', 'um'), and lack of linking between words.

intermediate.criteria: Moderate speech rate with some self-corrections or hesitations, but mostly reads and answers in complete, cohesive phrases.

advanced.criteria: Fluent, continuous speech at a natural tempo with appropriate grouping of words (phrasing) and natural linking between words.

tenses.what_is_measured: Correct usage and conjugation of verb tenses (Present, Past, Future, and Continuous) in speech.

beginner.criteria: Frequently uses the base verb form for all tenses (e.g. 'Yesterday I go'), misses auxiliary verbs, or mixes past and present forms incorrectly.

intermediate.criteria: Constructs simple past, present, and future tenses correctly, but commits errors in irregular verbs or continuous forms under cognitive load.

advanced.criteria: Flawless transitions between tenses and accurate conjugations of both regular and irregular verbs in spontaneous answers.

subject_verb_agreement.what_is_measured: Matching singular subjects with singular verbs and plural subjects with plural verbs (particularly 3rd person singular -s).

beginner.criteria: Consistent agreement errors (e.g. 'He go to school', 'My friends is here', 'She like coffee').

intermediate.criteria: Maintains agreement for basic subjects, but makes errors with collective nouns, compound subjects, or when clauses separate subject and verb.

advanced.criteria: Consistently correct subject-verb agreement across all sentence structures.

articles.what_is_measured: Proper use of definite ('the'), indefinite ('a', 'an'), and zero articles before nouns.

beginner.criteria: Regularly omits articles entirely (e.g. 'I want buy car') or uses 'a' and 'an' incorrectly before vowel/consonant sounds.

intermediate.criteria: Uses 'a/an' correctly, but struggles with the subtle difference between definite ('the') and indefinite articles in context, or uses articles where none are needed.

advanced.criteria: Precise, native-like application of article rules and exceptions in spontaneous speech.

prepositions.what_is_measured: Accurate selection of prepositions of place, time, and direction (e.g. in, on, at, under, to, through).

beginner.criteria: Omission or random substitution of prepositions (e.g., saying 'I am at the room' or 'He came on 5 PM').

intermediate.criteria: Accurate with basic prepositions of location and time, but errs with prepositional phrases, collocations (e.g., 'depend on' vs 'depend of'), or complex spatial descriptions.

advanced.criteria: Natural and correct use of spatial, temporal, and collocated prepositions throughout speech.

sentence_structure.what_is_measured: Basic word order (Subject-Verb-Object), and division of sentences into complete subjects and predicates without fragments or run-ons.

beginner.criteria: Uses fragmented phrases, disjointed structures, or word order transferred from their native language (e.g. Subject-Object-Verb).

intermediate.criteria: Constructs solid, complete simple sentences, but occasional run-on sentences or minor syntax alignment errors occur when joining clauses.

advanced.criteria: Maintains correct word order and clear subject-predicate structures across all spoken utterances.

question_formation.what_is_measured: Ability to construct grammatically correct direct and indirect questions, including auxiliary inversion and Wh-question words.

beginner.criteria: Forms questions using statement word order with rising intonation only (e.g. 'You like coffee?'), or fails to invert auxiliary verbs (e.g. 'Why you are here?').

intermediate.criteria: Constructs simple questions correctly, but struggles with complex do-support, double negatives, or indirect questions (e.g., 'Can you tell me where is the bus stop?').

advanced.criteria: Accurately forms direct and indirect questions using correct auxiliary inversion, question words, and tense structures.

complex_sentences.what_is_measured: Ability to formulate complex sentences using coordinating and subordinating conjunctions (because, although, since, if, relative pronouns) to link clauses.

beginner.criteria: Expresses thoughts in simple, short, disconnected sentences. Conjunctions are absent or restricted to 'and' / 'but'.

intermediate.criteria: Attempts complex sentences with basic sub-ordinators ('because', 'if') but makes clause structure, word order, or tense errors in conditional clauses.

advanced.criteria: Skillfully uses diverse subordinating conjunctions and relative clauses to construct grammatically sound complex sentences.

focus_areas: Past vs. present vs. future auxiliaries
Prepositions of place, time, and direction
